gṛhastha
(‘one [who is] established in a home’, ‘a married person or a householder’.)
------------------------------------------
See ĀŚRAMA.

Gṛhyasūtras
------------------------------------------
The वेदस्, the basic scriptures of हिन्दुइस्म्, are considered ‘apauruṣeya’ (not man-made but revealed). Couched in an archaic language they are often difficult to decipher or comprehend. Hence the six वेदाङ्गस् (‘limbs of the वेदस्’), six subsidiary sciences that help unfold the Vedic wisdom, came into existence.
Out of these six वेदाङ्गस्, the कल्प is the last. ‘Kalpa’ means ‘prayoga’ or practical method of doing a thing. It has, again, four branches: śrauta, gṛhya, धर्म and śulba. All these four are in the form of sūtras composed by different authors.
The गृह्यसूत्रस्, the second in the series, deal with the various rites to be performed in one’s gṛha or होउसे, such as the sixteen सṁस्कारस् like उपनयन, विवाह and others.
A list of the गृह्यसूत्रस् belonging to the four Vedic traditions, as available now, may now be given:—
Ṛgveda:Āśvalāyana Gṛhyasūtras
Śāṅkhāyana Gṛhyasūtras Śukla यजुर्वेद:Pāraskara Gṛhyasūtras Kṛṣṇa यजुर्वेद:Āpastamba Gṛhyasūtras
Baudhāyana Gṛhyasūtras
Bharadvāja Gṛhyasūtra Sāmaveda:Gobhila Gṛhyasūtras
Jaiminīya Gṛhyasūtras
Khādira Gṛhyasūtras Atharvaveda:Kauśika Gṛhyasūtras See under each title for more details.

gṛhapraveśa
(‘entering a [new] होउसे’)
------------------------------------------
A distinguishing feature in a Hindu’s life is that no action of his is divorced from religion. Starting from personal cleanliness and hygiene as a part of daily routine, right up to the time of going to bed or even up to death, everything he is expected to do, has to have a religious colour or flavour.
Building a new होउसे and entering it is one of the most important occasions in the life of a गृहस्थ or a householder. Naturally, this has to be done in a befitting manner. The गृह्यसूत्रस् as also the धर्मशास्त्रस् prescribe elaborate procedures for this ceremony called ‘gṛha-praveśa’ or ceremonially entering the होउसे.
It may not be out of place to mention here that when लक्ष्मण built a parṇa-kuṭi (a thatched होउसे) for राम, सीता and himself to live, in चित्रकूट, an elabo-rate गृहप्रवेश ceremony was performed (Rāmāyaṇa, Ayodhyākāṇḍa, 56.22-35).
A गृहप्रवेश is of four types:
Entering an old होउसे by the new master who has acquired it.
Entering a renovated होउसे by the same owner.
Entering a newly built होउसे by its owner.
Entering one’s own (old) होउसे after a long lapse of time due to पिल्ग्रिमगे and so on.
Of these, it is really the third one that is treated more elaborately as गृहप्रवेश in the true sense.
Before performing गृहप्रवेश, an auspicious day according to the traditional Hindu चलेन्दर् has to be fixed. On the previous night, Rākṣoghna-होम has to be performed to ward off the evil spirits that might have been living there since a long time.
The first thing to be done is the worship of the वास्तुपुरुष, the cosmic man embodying the whole च्रेअतिओन्, including the different deities of the Hindu pantheon. For this, a Vāstumaṇḍala (a geometrical drawing, square in shape, containing 9 x 9 = 81 small squares) has to be drawn at an appropriate place in the होउसे and decorated with coloured powders. This has to be followed by Vāstu-होम, worship of the नवग्रहस् (the nine प्लनेत्स्) and of गणपति, the lord of (and destroyer of) obstacles as also पूर्णाहुति (the final oblation).
A long cotton thread is then wound round the होउसे thrice to make it secure—this is called ‘digbandhana’ or ‘locking the quarters’—followed by balis or offerings to the guardian deities like इन्द्र. A बलि is offered to the वास्तुपुरुष also.
The owner, then, has to ceremonially enter the होउसे along with his wife. The procession should comprise instrumental मुसिच्, Vedic chanting, पूर्णकुम्भ (holy water pot), certain auspicious materials like milk and butter, suvāsinīs (married ladies whose husbands are alive), images of gods, images of the family deities, a cow and its calf. The cow and the calf are taken in first and led up to the place where the family shrine is to be established. After establishing the family deities there, a simple worship is done. The ब्राह्मण priests are then honoured and given presents. Guests are also fed sumptuously.
Writing of Oṁ (Praṇava), the स्वस्तिक symbol, letters and words like ‘śrīḥ,’ ‘gaṇeśāya namaḥ’ (preferably in Sanskrit) on the walls of the new होउसे as also boiling milk in a pot and make it overflow are other local customs present in some parts of the country.

gṛhakarman
(‘the act of building a होउसे’)
------------------------------------------
Any householder, who could afford it, was expected to build a होउसे for himself and his family. However, he was to observe certain rules and regulations in doing so.
A place where the earth is whitish in colour and the ground is level, is considered suitable.
As regards the wood to be used, the following are to be avoided: wood of a tree from which its milk is oozing out; trees on which birds are living; trees which have fallen to the ground or those which have been burnt; trees grown in the premises of temples; trees in which deities or divine beings are believed to reside; thorny trees.
As regards digging a well inside one’s compound, certain directions like south-east and north-west were prohibited. On the other hand, east, west and north were recommended.
Houses could be begun to built in certain auspicious months only like Vaiśākha (April/May) or आषाढ (July/ August) and not in the inauspicious ones like चैत्र (March/April) or Māgha (February/March).
More details have been provided in the science called ‘Vāstuśāstra.’ Certain पुराणस् also deal with this subject.
